mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals labor market overheating, which historically precedes Fed tightening and reduced corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1.5% or more over two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by 1.5% or more for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the average return is not significantly negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the average return is not significantly negative at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both personal savings (RSAFS) and personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above their respective 12-month averages signals a rebalancing toward spending after a savings-driven period, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and GDPC1 both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered months, or the average return is not significantly positive at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate profit growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly positive at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) of 10% or more from the previous month signals a sharp contraction in residential investment, which reduces GDP growth and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by 10% or more month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.
